stories.label: Anti-Ankara fighters evacuate four bases in Iraq's north
stories.summary: Turkey's intelligence service confirmed on Monday that PKK fighters have withdrawn from four key bases in northern Iraq, the move the group announced last week, two months after Ankara's parliament passed a limited amnesty for its militants. Lead with the confirmation and the four bases (name them and where they are if the page does). The mechanism: a four-decade insurgency that cost some 40,000 lives is being wound down in steps, each side verifying the other: the PKK's dissolution, the amnesty law, now the bases; say what the amnesty covers and excludes, who takes over the vacated ground (Iraqi federal forces, the Kurdistan Region's peshmerga, Turkish troops already inside Iraq), and what Ankara still demands. Who it lands on: villagers in Duhok and Erbil provinces displaced by years of Turkish air strikes, and Kurds in Turkey waiting on the political half of the bargain. Give the PKK's own statement and Baghdad's if the page has them. It is agency copy carried by Dawn; no Turkish or Iraqi outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline, naming the PKK. Dateline Ankara.

stories.label: Scores of PTI workers held in crackdown across KP
stories.summary: New since the 11 October pieces on the emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the assembly bans in Peshawar, Lahore and Karachi (one clause): the arrests have begun. Scores of PTI workers were detained across the province on Monday, and a case was registered in Swat against two PTI members of the National Assembly, four provincial legislators and dozens of workers over a rally held on 28 September, before the emergency existed. Lead with the detentions (how many, in which districts, on what charges) and the legislators named. The mechanism: governor's rule removed the elected PTI provincial government, and the police and prosecution it controlled now answer to the centre, so old rallies become new cases; the same day the law department dismissed 57 of the province's law officers and appointed 27 (Dawn, https://www.dawn.com/news/2036701 if the writer finds it; otherwise one clause from this page only), and opposition members in the Balochistan Assembly demanded the PTI government be restored (https://www.dawn.com/news/2036756). Give the government's stated grounds and PTI's reply. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet and the only source. Write your own headline, spelling out Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Dateline Peshawar, or Swat if the page is filed from there.

stories.label: Catholics in US Army must not participate in firing squad, prominent archbishop says
stories.summary: Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who oversees the pastoral care of Catholics in the US armed forces, has said Catholic soldiers must not take part in the firing squad for Hasan, the former Army officer who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, and objected to what Reuters calls an unprecedented plan to broadcast the execution. Lead with the instruction and its target: a senior churchman telling serving soldiers to refuse an order. The mechanism: say what the Army plans (the method, the date, the broadcast and who ordered it, only as the page gives it), that the US military has not executed anyone since 1961, what Catholic teaching on the death penalty has said since 2018, and what military law offers a soldier who refuses on conscience. The reader's stake: the condemned man is a Muslim American whose crime was used for years against Muslims in uniform, and the state now proposes to make his death a broadcast; report that plainly and give the Pentagon's and the victims' families' statements as the page has them. It is Reuters copy carried by Daily Maverick. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: UK growth upgraded but energy prices and rates to bite in 2027
stories.summary: New since Sunday's curtain-raiser on the IMF meetings in Bangkok (one clause): the forecasts are out. The IMF's World Economic Outlook raises 2026 world growth to 3.1% while warning that the economy's resilience is waning, and it has sharply cut its 2026 projections for the Gulf economies because the Strait of Hormuz has stayed closed, pushing back the date it assumes the waterway reopens (The National). Lead with that pair, not with Britain: a higher global number beside deep cuts for the exporters whose oil cannot leave. The mechanism: growth this year was pulled forward by investment and stockpiling, and the bill arrives in 2027 as dear energy and higher interest rates bite; give the Gulf figures country by country as The National has them, the old and new assumption on Hormuz, and one sentence on Britain (upgraded for 2026, cut for 2027) from the BBC. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the price of Brent crude and the Fed's interest rate. Who it lands on: Gulf budgets and the migrant workers they pay, and fuel importers in Asia and Africa. These are forecasts: state them as the IMF's. TRT World is Turkish state media, used where the others agree. Write your own headline about the global and Gulf forecasts. Dateline Bangkok.

stories.label: Oil shipping and insurance costs exceed one-third of the commodity value -- OPEC
stories.summary: Ministers of OPEC and its allies say the cost of shipping and insuring oil has reached more than one third of the value of the cargo, a level they call unprecedented and one that is 'impeding' the movement of crude and products. Lead with the fraction: on a barrel near $105, over $35 now goes to freight and war-risk cover before it reaches a refinery. The mechanism: three tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz in two days, the Houthis threaten the Red Sea route, and underwriters reprice every voyage, so the price a producer receives and the price an importer pays have come apart; say what normal freight-and-insurance shares are, as the page gives them, what the ministers asked for or decided, and where they met. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Distinct from Monday's piece on OPEC's demand forecast (one clause). Who it lands on: importers in South Asia and Africa who pay the delivered price, and the seafarers the premium is priced on. The accountability point: several of the ministers' own governments are parties to the war that set the premium. Write from Reuters; TASS is Russian state media, used only for quoted remarks. Write your own headline. Dateline as Reuters places the meeting.

stories.label: Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeps alive BOJ rate-hike view
stories.summary: Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September, slower than in August but high enough to keep a near-term Bank of Japan rate rise in view. Lead with the figure and what it measures: the prices companies charge each other, which reach shop shelves months later. The mechanism: Japan imports almost all its energy, much of it through the Strait of Hormuz, and pays for it in a weak yen, so the oil shock and the currency compound in import prices; give the yen-based import price index, the oil and telecoms components and the previous month's figure as the page has them, then the Bank of Japan's current policy rate, its next meeting date and what a rise would do to the yen and to a government carrying the rich world's largest debt. Name the series plainly: the yen and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: Japanese households whose wages trail prices. Attribute expectations of a rate rise to the markets and analysts Reuters cites; state none as fact. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: 'Pakistan's poverty rate higher than India, B'desh'
stories.summary: More than one third of Pakistan's population lives in multidimensional poverty, overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards, a higher share than in India or Bangladesh, according to the UNDP's Multidimensional Poverty Index released on Monday. Lead with Pakistan's share and headcount beside its two neighbours' figures. The mechanism for a general reader: the index does not count income; it counts households that lack several things at once (a child out of school, a death of a child, no electricity, clean water or cooking fuel), which is why it can diverge from the dollar-a-day measure; say which indicators drive Pakistan's score, how the provinces differ, the survey years behind each country's figure (they differ, and it limits the comparison), and the global totals the report gives for South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. The structural point: three countries that began from one starting line in 1947 and 1971 have separated on schooling and child survival; give what the report and the Pakistani officials quoted attribute it to, and no more. Attribute all figures to the UNDP. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet and the only source. Write your own headline, spelling out Bangladesh. Dateline as Dawn files it (the report was released in New York); do not count it as a US story.

stories.label: 20个中国品牌挤进巴黎车展，欧洲车企坐不住了
stories.summary: Twenty Chinese car brands are exhibiting at the Paris Motor Show, and TMTPost, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports that European carmakers are finding that home advantage is 'becoming less reliable'. Lead with the count and what it was at the last show. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which brands came and with what (battery-electric, plug-in hybrid, range-extender; prices in euros against European rivals; charging speeds, driver-assistance and software the piece cites), how they get round the EU's tariffs on Chinese-made electric cars (hybrids, which the tariff does not cover, and plants in Hungary, Spain or Turkey), and what Renault, Stellantis and Volkswagen showed in answer. One clause on Sunday's China-EU quota deal on hybrids, already covered. The value of this piece is the view from inside China's industry: say how the Chinese makers themselves describe the European market, including overcapacity and the price war at home that pushes them abroad, if the page says so. In Chinese; translate names and figures exactly, attribute to TMTPost, and state its characterisations as its own. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: PAC-3 Edge Will Be The Most Capable Patriot Interceptor Ever
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin has unveiled the PAC-3 Edge, a new interceptor to sit at the top of the Patriot family with more range, altitude and manoeuvrability than the PAC-3 MSE. Lead with what it is and what it is for, stated as the maker's claims. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what changes (motor, seeker, hit-to-kill against which classes of threat: manoeuvring ballistic missiles, hypersonic glide vehicles), whether it fits existing launchers and radars, when it is due and who is paying for development, as the page gives it. The structural point is arithmetic, not performance: Patriot batteries are what stands between Iranian and Houthi missiles and Gulf cities and airports, each interceptor costs millions of dollars against far cheaper attackers, and production of the current round already trails what the Gulf war and Ukraine consume; say what the page gives on output and stockpiles, and that a more capable round is also a costlier and scarcer one. The War Zone is a specialist defence outlet: no performance claim beyond what Lockheed states, attributed. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the unveiling. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Order No. 837: Beijing’s rules for China’s rocket exporters
stories.summary: Beijing has issued Order No. 837, a set of rules governing how China's commercial rocket companies may sell launches and hardware abroad. Lead with the order itself: who issued it, when it takes effect and what it requires of a private launch firm before it can export (licences, state review of customers and technology, as the page gives them). The mechanism for a technical reader: China's 'commercial' launch sector (name the firms the piece names) grew on state engines, state launch sites and provincial money, and the order writes that dependence into export law, so the companies compete for foreign customers as arms of a state system, not as a Chinese SpaceX; say what that means for a buyer in the Gulf, Africa or Southeast Asia choosing between a Chinese launch and an American one under ITAR. One clause on Monday's piece on Kyrgyzstan's satellite only if the page draws a link. The Lowy Interpreter is a think-tank publication and this is analysis: report the order's provisions as facts where the piece documents them, and attribute the reading ('folding entrepreneurial firms into a wider state system') to its author by name. The feed entry is a one-line teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Fire erupts in tanker after being hit by projectile in Hormuz
stories.summary: New since Sunday's pieces on Iran rejecting the US reply and the Guards' claim that a second tanker struck a mine (one clause): the IRGC navy says a third supertanker it calls 'offending' was hit in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday morning and caught fire, the third in two days. Lead with the count and the fire, attributed to the IRGC statement, and say what is independently known: the ship's name, flag, cargo and crew, who or what struck it (the Guards say 'projectile', earlier 'mine'), and what CENTCOM or UK maritime authorities have confirmed or denied, as The National gives it. The mechanism: Iran is enforcing its own rules of passage by naming ships 'offending' and letting them burn, while US forces fire on blockade runners, so two blockades now overlap in one channel and insurers price both. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: the crews, mostly South and Southeast Asian seafarers, and fuel importers in Asia. Mehr is Iranian state media and Middle East Monitor is relaying Anadolu (Turkish state media): state the strike as the Guards' claim unless The National confirms it. Write your own headline. Dateline as the reports place it (Tehran for the statement).

stories.label: Russia warned NATO is 'ready to fight tonight' as WW3 fears skyrocket
stories.summary: NATO's top commander, the US general Alexus Grynkewich, used the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday to lay out how the alliance would stop a Russian attack, saying it would do 'anything and everything' if attacked while adding that he does not think war is imminent or inevitable. Lead with what he actually set out, not the tabloid framing: the plan's elements as the New York Times, AFP and Al Jazeera give them (forces, drones, the answer to sabotage, open lines to Moscow to 'resolve misunderstandings'), and what he declined to specify. The mechanism: deterrence is being restated in public in Warsaw, days after the arrest over a plot against Tusk and attacks on Polish schools, and while Washington's commitment is in question over the Russian diesel deal and the threat to halt PURL arms; say what the plan assumes about US forces and what European members must supply. Sentiment diverges (0.45): the Express and Mint play it as war warning, the NYT as strategy; say what is established and what is tone. Give Moscow's reply if a page has it. The Express is a tabloid and the feed's lead link: write from the NYT, AFP (Yahoo) and Al Jazeera, and write your own headline with no 'WW3'. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: Elon Musk spends $366 million on 2026 US midterm elections
stories.summary: Elon Musk is the largest single donor of the 2026 US midterms, with hundreds of millions of dollars spent for Republicans three weeks before the vote. The sources disagree on the figure: the New York Post's own URL and text say $276 million, its headline and Al Jazeera say $366 million; lead with the number the filings support, say which filing or count each figure comes from, and state the discrepancy plainly if it cannot be resolved. The mechanism: say through which vehicles the money moved (his own PAC, party committees, direct support in House and Senate races, as the pages give it), what US law caps and what it leaves uncapped since Citizens United, and how the sum compares with the next-largest donor and with his 2024 spending. The accountability point: one man whose companies hold federal contracts and face federal regulators is financing the party that controls both; say what contracts or agencies the pages name, and no more. Give the Democrats' and Musk's own statements. Write from Al Jazeera first; the New York Post is a tabloid close to the Republican side. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Tiguerones Leader ‘Willy’ Is Living Free in Spain
stories.summary: William Joffre Alcívar Bautista, 'Willy', the alleged leader of the Tiguerones, one of Ecuador's most powerful gangs and a group the US has designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization, is living free in Spain while Ecuadorian authorities still seek him, InSight Crime reports. Lead with that contradiction. The mechanism: say how he got to Spain and on what legal footing he stays (an asylum claim, a refused or stalled extradition, a release by a Spanish court, as the piece documents it), what Ecuador has charged him with, and why a US terrorist designation does not bind a Spanish judge. The structural point: Ecuador's 'internal armed conflict' against its gangs stops at the border, and the leaders who can afford to leave run or outlast it from Europe, the same Europe that is the market for the cocaine moving through Guayaquil. Give the replies of the Spanish and Ecuadorian authorities and of Alcívar's lawyers, or say they did not answer. InSight Crime is an investigative outlet: attribute every finding to it and state allegations as allegations. Single source. Dateline as the report places him in Spain, with Ecuador's side given its own voice.

stories.label: In this West Bank village, Israel won’t let Palestinians visit their dead
stories.summary: Since August, Israeli settlers have blocked the Palestinian residents of Umm Safa, a village north of Ramallah, from reaching its only cemetery, Mondoweiss reports from the village; residents say the army backs the settlers and that it is the latest step in an effort to drive them out. Lead with the cemetery: who is kept from it, since when, and by what means (an outpost, a gate, armed men, a military order, as the piece gives it), and where the village now buries its dead. The mechanism: say how the closure fits the sequence the residents describe (land seized, roads closed, attacks), what legal status the settlers' presence has under Israeli and international law, and what the army and the Civil Administration say, or that they did not answer. Name the villagers quoted and the settlers or outpost where named. This is ground reportage: attribute findings to Mondoweiss and the people it quotes. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. No regional outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Umm Safa.

stories.label: Nigeria records 268 Lassa fever deaths as fatality rate rises to 23.6%- NCDC
stories.summary: Lassa fever has killed 268 people in Nigeria this year and is killing a larger share of those it infects: the case fatality rate is 23.6%, against 18.6% in the same period of 2025, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control says, even as new confirmed cases fell sharply in the latest reporting week. Lead with the two rates: nearly one confirmed patient in four dies. The mechanism: say what Lassa is in one sentence (a haemorrhagic fever carried by rats, endemic in West Africa, with no licensed vaccine), then why the death rate rises while cases fall, as the NCDC explains it: late presentation, the cost of treatment, too few treatment centres; give confirmed and suspected cases, the states that carry most of them (Benue is tagged), and health-worker infections. Who it lands on: rural households in a handful of states. Set it beside the same day's news that Nigeria is to take over its health financing from donors (one clause). Premium Times is the Nigerian outlet and the only source; attribute figures to the NCDC. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: FG to invest $3bn into health sector by 2030
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government says it will put an additional $3 billion into its health sector by 2030 under a transition arrangement with the United States, in which the two countries work toward Nigeria financing its health system entirely by itself by that year, the health minister, Muhammad Ali Pate, said. Lead with the sum and the end date, then what it replaces: say what the memorandum with Washington commits each side to, how much US money (PEPFAR and the rest) has paid for HIV, TB and malaria programmes and how fast it tapers, as the page gives it. The mechanism: a donor is exiting on a schedule and writing the recipient's budget line into the agreement; say where the $3 billion is to come from in a budget strained by debt service and a weak naira, and what share of Nigerian health spending is now out of pocket, only as the piece supports it. Who it lands on: the patients on donor-funded antiretrovirals and the clinics that dispense them. This is a pledge: state it as the government's. Premium Times is the Nigerian outlet and the only source. Write your own headline, spelling out 'federal government'. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: Hong Kong to expand indices, derivatives and yuan-denominated products: HKEX CEO
stories.summary: Hong Kong's exchange operator, HKEX, plans to add yuan-denominated gold futures and yuan stock trading, along with new indices and derivatives, its chief executive wrote on Monday. Lead with the yuan products, which are the part that matters outside Hong Kong: gold and shares priced and settled in China's currency on an exchange open to foreign investors. The mechanism: the yuan is not freely convertible, so Beijing internationalises it through Hong Kong, where offshore yuan can be held, traded and hedged; each new product gives holders of the currency something to do with it other than sell it for dollars. Say what exists already (the dual-counter share scheme, Stock Connect), what is new, the timetable and what needs regulators' approval, as the page gives it. Name the series plainly: the yuan and the price of gold. These are an exchange's stated plans, not launched products: say so, and attribute to the chief executive's post. Single source. Dateline Hong Kong.

stories.label: Meta Says New Muse Model Reaches AI Frontier After 14-Month Push
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on how ByteDance and Tencent answered Meta's Muse agent (one clause): Meta on Monday released Muse Wonder, the model it calls its most capable and says reaches the frontier, the first real test of the multibillion-dollar rebuilding of its AI organisation that began 14 months ago. Lead with the release and the claim, stated as Meta's. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the model is (sizes, modalities, context, whether weights are open or it is API-only, a break with Meta's open Llama line if so), which benchmarks Meta cites and who ran them, the price, and where it ships (Meta's own apps, an API). Then the cost of getting here: the hiring spree, the reorganisation and the capital spending, in the figures the pages give. Self-reported benchmarks are claims, not results: say what independent evaluation exists, or that none does yet. Bloomberg is paywalled and the other two cluster links are investor notes (an analyst rating and a stock explainer): use them for facts about the release only, with no price targets or stock commentary. Dateline Menlo Park. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Report: Epic Games goes all-in on AI for Disney collaboration
stories.summary: Epic Games is building its Disney shooter 'AI first', with AI models writing all the code and guiding all the artwork, according to a Bloomberg report that Ars Technica relays, citing unnamed people familiar with the project. Lead with 'all the code', attributed. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what 'AI first' means in the studio's pipeline as described (which models, what humans still do: review, direction, integration), how large the team is against a conventional production of that size, and what Epic and Disney said when asked. The structural point: this is one of the industry's largest studios, the maker of Unreal Engine and Fortnite, on a flagship licence from the company most protective of its characters, after two years of mass layoffs in games; say what the unions and the developers quoted fear, and what copyright question AI-generated Disney art raises, only as the page supports it. It is a report from unnamed sources, relayed second-hand: attribute throughout and state nothing as confirmed that Epic has not confirmed. Single source. Dateline Cary, North Carolina, if the report places Epic there. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: The Mystery of Kyrgyzstan’s Newly Launched Satellite(s)
stories.summary: Kyrgyzstan announced the launch of a satellite as a national achievement, and then, The Diplomat reports, the official story changed: how many satellites there were, who built them and whose they are no longer add up. Lead with the discrepancy in plain words: what was first announced, by whom, and what was said later. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what was actually launched (size, type, orbit, launch provider and date), who designed, built and paid for it, and what can be checked independently from launch manifests and tracking catalogues against the government's account. The structural point: a small state buys or borrows a satellite and presents it as home-built capability, and the gap shows when the paperwork is public. Distinct from this afternoon's piece on the 'national' electric-car plant tied to the presidential property office (one clause at most, and only if the article draws the link). Give the officials' explanations as the page has them. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. No Kyrgyz outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Dateline Bishkek.

stories.label: UK Says Iran's IRGC Directed Incident at Airbase Used by US
stories.summary: Britain's prime minister, Andy Burnham, told MPs the alleged terror plot at RAF Fairford, the British base US bombers fly from, was 'highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by' the Revolutionary Guards. Lead with the attribution, quoted exactly, and with what it rests on: an intelligence assessment, not a court finding; say what actually happened at the base, who has been arrested or charged, and what Britain does next (sanctions, proscribing the IRGC, as the pages give it), plus Tehran's reply. The mechanism: a base in England used for the US war on Iran makes Britain a party in Tehran's eyes, and the attribution moves London toward measures it has long held back from. Distinct from this morning's piece on Burnham and Russia's Brexit interference (one clause at most). State allegations as allegations. Bloomberg is paywalled: write from SCMP and TRT World (Turkish state media, used where the others agree). Dateline London.

stories.label: Photos: Protests over voter lists escalate in India's capital
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on Delhi Police striking Jantar Mantar off the list of protest sites, which said Rahul Gandhi was to march on the Supreme Court (one clause): the march happened. Thousands marched in New Delhi on Monday demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the voter-roll revision, in what Al Jazeera calls the latest confrontation with authorities in a heavily fortified capital. Lead with the march itself: how many, by whose count, where police stopped it, how many were detained or hurt, and whether it reached the court. The mechanism for a reader outside India: say in two sentences what the roll revision did (who was struck off, and how many, as the pages give it) and why the opposition calls it 'vote theft', then what the Election Commission and the government answer. Write from Dawn's report and the captions of the Al Jazeera gallery; the Guardian link is an editorial, usable only as attributed opinion. Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: South Korea Recalls Ambassador, Demands Public Apology From Ukraine
stories.summary: Seoul has recalled its ambassador from Kyiv and is demanding a public apology after Ukraine made public a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war that South Korea wanted kept quiet. Lead with the recall and the demand, then what Kyiv disclosed and when. The mechanism: South Korea's constitution treats North Koreans as its own citizens, so captured soldiers who ask to go south are a quiet channel Seoul wants to keep open, and publicity endangers the men's families in the North and hands Pyongyang a grievance, days after it fired missiles; say why Kyiv went public anyway and what it gains. Give both governments' statements and what the rift does to South Korean aid or arms for Ukraine, only as the page has it. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. Single source. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: In Yemen, No One Wants To Be a Teacher Anymore
stories.summary: Yemen's teacher-training colleges are emptying: some departments now enrol no students at all, New Lines reports from Mukalla, where a dean sits in a classroom that held more than 100 students in 1996. Lead with that zero and the classroom. The mechanism: a teacher's salary is paid in a riyal that has collapsed, while armed forces on every side pay recruits more and in harder currency, so the young men who would have taught enlist instead; give the salary and exchange-rate figures and the enrolment numbers by college and year as the piece has them, and name the Yemeni rial plainly. Who it lands on: a generation of children with no one trained to teach them, a cost of the war that outlasts any ceasefire. One clause on the fighting now moving toward Bab al-Mandeb. It is ground reportage: attribute findings to New Lines and the people it quotes. No regional outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Mukalla.

stories.label: What’s behind Venezuela’s mounting electricity crisis?
stories.summary: Venezuela's blackouts are worsening, and the report traces them to corruption, years without maintenance and the emigration of the engineers who ran the grid. Lead with the present state of supply: how many hours of cuts, in which states, affecting how many people, as the page gives it. The mechanism: the country depends on one hydroelectric complex (Guri) and long transmission lines, the thermal plants meant to back it up were paid for and never finished or left to decay, and the skilled staff left with the wider exodus; give the figures for installed against working capacity and name the contracts or officials the piece names, as allegations where they are. Who it lands on: hospitals, water pumping and households in the west of the country, far from Caracas. Say what the government blames (sabotage, sanctions) and what the piece's sources answer. Single source; write only what it supports. Write your own headline. Dateline Caracas.

stories.label: South Korea just got its first traditional bank loans backed by bitcoin
stories.summary: Jeonbuk Bank has begun lending cash to companies against their bitcoin, the first South Korean bank to accept crypto as loan collateral, and it is doing so under existing law, with no new rule passed. Lead with the product and that last fact. The mechanism for a technical reader: say who holds the coins while the loan runs (which custodian), the loan-to-value ratio, what happens when the price of bitcoin falls (margin call, forced sale), and why only corporate clients qualify; then what the regulator has said. The structural point: collateral is how an asset's volatility enters a bank's balance sheet, and a regional bank has opened that door in one of the world's most active crypto markets without a legislative decision. Name the series plainly: the price of bitcoin. CoinDesk is a trade outlet: no price commentary and no adoption forecasts stated as fact. Single source. Dateline Seoul, or Jeonju if the report places the bank there.

stories.label: Bangladesh-Malaysia recruitment reforms revive old questions over the cost of migration
stories.summary: Bangladesh and Malaysia have again rewritten the rules for sending Bangladeshi workers to Malaysia, and the same problems the earlier agreements left standing are back in question: a 'syndicate' of favoured recruiting agencies, fees many times the legal cap, and abuse on arrival. Lead with what the new reform changes and what a worker actually pays to go against what the law allows, in taka and ringgit as the page gives them. The mechanism: the Malaysian side approves only a short list of Bangladeshi agencies, the scarcity of slots is sold down a chain of sub-agents, and the worker borrows to pay it, arriving in debt bondage before the first wage; say who is on the list, who chose it, and what earlier investigations or the UN have found. Who it lands on: hundreds of thousands of Bangladeshi workers whose remittances both economies depend on. Name the Bangladeshi taka plainly if the piece gives costs in it. Both governments are named actors: give their replies. No Bangladeshi or Malaysian outlet in the feed carries it. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Dhaka.

stories.label: Study links environment and youth mental health
stories.summary: A University of Canterbury-led study followed almost 1 million young New Zealanders, close to the country's whole youth population, and found that the places they live in are linked to their mental health over time. Lead with the scale and the finding in plain words: which features of a neighbourhood (green and blue space, fast-food and alcohol outlets, gambling venues, as the page names them) went with better or worse outcomes, and by how much. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how it was done (linked national administrative data, how mental health was measured, how environments were scored, the years covered) and what was controlled for, notably deprivation. This is an association, not a demonstrated cause: say so, and give the limits the authors state. Why it matters: it is evidence for planning decisions, and health-harming outlets cluster in poorer areas. Name Dr Lukáš Marek, the journal and the funder. It is a press-release rewrite: read the page and, if it links the paper, claim no more than the paper does. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Christchurch.

stories.label: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones have knocked out three of the largest data centres owned by Yandex, the third over the weekend, and cloud services, payments, deliveries and other online services are failing across Russia. Lead with the three sites and what stopped working for ordinary users. The mechanism for a technical reader: Russia opened this front by striking Ukrainian data centres and telecoms, but Ukraine had already moved state systems to foreign clouds, while sanctions left Russia concentrated in a few domestic facilities with no hyperscaler abroad to fail over to; say where the sites are, what they hosted (the feed tags a supercomputer), how far the drones flew, and how long recovery is expected to take, as Ars and The Record give it. The structural point: a data centre is now a military target like a refinery, and digital sovereignty turned out to be a single point of failure. One sentence from netzpolitik.org (in German): the rumour that the strikes silenced pro-AfD social bots has no evidence behind it. Give Yandex's and Moscow's statements. The Record's entry is a teaser. Write your own headline. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: European U740 Variant Of The XQ-58A Valkyrie Has Flown
stories.summary: The U740, a European version of the American XQ-58A Valkyrie combat drone built by Airbus with the US firm Kratos, has made its first flight, as Germany pushes to field uncrewed combat aircraft by 2029. Lead with the flight (where, when, what was tested) and the deadline. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what a 'loyal wingman' is, a jet-powered drone cheap enough to lose that flies with crewed fighters, what Airbus changed from the American airframe (mission system, sensors, weapons, European control of the software), and why Berlin bought a flying US design instead of waiting for a European one. The structural point: Europe's rearmament says it wants independence from Washington and is being built on licensed American hardware, because the home-grown programme (FCAS) is years late; say what that leaves under US export control, only as the page supports it. The War Zone is a specialist defence outlet: no performance claim beyond what the makers state, attributed. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the flight.

stories.label: Immigration officials search Congresswoman Ilhan Omar home
stories.summary: Homeland Security Investigations agents searched the Washington home of Ilhan Omar, a sitting Democratic congresswoman and one of the first Muslim women in Congress, on Monday morning under what DHS calls a 'judicially authorized search' in a criminal probe. Lead with the search and what is and is not known: which agency, which court issued the warrant, what the investigation concerns (only as NBC and the BBC give it, attributed to named or unnamed sources as they are), and whether Omar has been charged with anything (say plainly if not). The mechanism: an immigration-enforcement arm of the executive, under a president who has attacked Omar by name for years, is investigating an opposition legislator three weeks before the midterms; say what the Constitution's Speech or Debate clause does and does not protect, what Omar, House Democratic leaders and the White House have said, and what precedent there is for searching a sitting member's home. State allegations as allegations. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: UK PM Andy Burnham says it is 'clear' Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
stories.summary: Britain's prime minister, Andy Burnham, says it is 'clear' Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum, and is telling MPs on parliament's return that it would be a 'dereliction of duty' to turn down a closer relationship with the EU if one can be negotiated. Lead with both halves together: a sitting prime minister is the first to state the interference as fact, and he says it on the day he opens the argument for moving back toward Brussels. Quote him exactly. The mechanism: say what evidence he cites (the 2020 Intelligence and Security Committee 'Russia report' found no government had looked for it; say whether anything new has been produced), what 'closer relationship' means in terms he has actually named (customs union, single market, a deal short of both), and what the Conservatives, Reform and the Kremlin have answered. Sentiment diverges sharply (0.66): the BBC treats it as a domestic row, Al Jazeera and Hindustan Times as a statement about Russia; say what is established and what is assertion. The BBC link is a liveblog: write from Al Jazeera and take only dated, attributed lines from the BBC page. Dateline London.

stories.label: Skies Over Saudi Capital Empty After Deadly Houthi Airport Strikes
stories.summary: New since the pieces on the two attacks on Riyadh's airport, the Houthis declaring all Saudi airports targets and the four-state demand that they stop (one clause): the threat has now done what it was meant to. Saudi authorities on Monday extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International, the kingdom's second-busiest airport, and Australia and New Zealand joined the United States and others in warning their citizens against travel to Saudi Arabia. Lead with the extended closure (until when, by whose order, as the pages give it) and the empty airspace over a capital of some eight million, then the advisories by country. The mechanism: an armed group has closed a G20 capital's airport with two strikes and an announcement, because airlines and insurers price the threat, not the hit rate; say which carriers have suspended or rerouted, what has happened to flights at Jeddah and to Umrah travel if a page says, and who is stranded, including the migrant workers from Pakistan, India and Bangladesh who are most of the airport's traffic (Dawn). Give the toll of the strikes as the Saudi aviation authority last stated it, attributed. Write from Al Jazeera and Dawn; Mehr is Iranian state media and calls the attackers 'Yemen', so use it only for the Saudi statement on the closure, attributed. Write your own headline. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Вывески меняются, но у приближенных Туманбаева все равно остается автозавод
stories.summary: Kyrgyzstan's economy ministry announced in August that the country would launch an electric-car plant under a 'national brand', BARS. Kloop, the independent Kyrgyz investigative outlet, reports that the plant was in fact built earlier by Chinese investors together with the presidential administration's property office and Module House, a company linked to that office's head, Kanybek Tumanbaev: 'the signs change', as its headline puts it, but the factory stays with his associates. Lead with the finding in plain words and with what Kloop documents it from (company registries, contracts, earlier names of the plant). The mechanism: a state body that manages the president's property goes into business alongside a private firm tied to its own chief, and the venture is then relaunched as a national industrial project with public backing; trace the ownership chain and the renamings step by step, name the Chinese partner, and say what state support, land or tax relief the plant has received. Give Tumanbaev's and the ministry's replies, or say they did not answer. The structural point: Chinese capital entering Central Asia through the households of those in power. In Russian; translate names and figures exactly, attribute every finding to Kloop and state allegations as allegations. Kloop is blocked and prosecuted in Kyrgyzstan (one clause, if the page says so). Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Bishkek.

stories.label: Fim da escala 6×1 pode ir a votação no Senado, mas aliados de Flávio tentam barrar
stories.summary: Brazil's Senate may vote on ending the '6x1' schedule, six days of work for one of rest, the legal norm for tens of millions of shop, restaurant and service workers, and allies of Flávio Bolsonaro are trying to keep it off the floor while he faces Lula in the presidential run-off. Lead with the measure and the manoeuvre: what the bill or constitutional amendment would change (the weekly hours cap and days off, as the page gives them), where it stands in the Senate, and who is blocking it and by what procedure. The mechanism for a reader outside Brazil: the 6x1 week is written into labour law from the 1940s, a movement that began on social media made its abolition a mass demand, and the vote now forces the right to choose between employers who oppose it and the working-class voters both candidates need; say what Lula's government, employer federations and the unions each say, and give the run-off date. Who it lands on: the workers on the schedule, disproportionately Black and female, if the page says so. In Portuguese; translate names and figures exactly and attribute to Agência Pública. It is a short note: write only what it supports. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Food inflation spikes to 7.74% in Sept
stories.summary: India's consumer inflation jumped to 5.54% in September, an almost two-year high, and food inflation to 7.74% from 5.97% in August, after seven months below zero that ended only last December. Lead with the two figures and the speed of the turn. The mechanism: say which foods drove it (vegetables, pulses, edible oil, as the pages give them) and why: an erratic monsoon in an El Niño year and fuel and fertiliser costs raised by the Gulf war; then what the Reserve Bank of India does with it, since Reuters and Bloomberg both read the number as strengthening the case for further rate rises, and give the current repo rate, the RBI's target band and the next meeting date. Who it lands on: households that spend close to half their budget on food, in a country of 1.4 billion, for whom a rate rise also means dearer loans. Attribute forecasts to the economists who make them and state none as fact. Financial Express carries the food breakdown; Bloomberg is paywalled. Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Global oil demand to grow by 0.4 mln barrels daily in 2026 -- OPEC Secretary General
stories.summary: OPEC has cut its forecast for growth in world oil demand this year to 400,000 barrels a day, well under what it expected in January, and says the missing consumption will return as 'pent-up demand' in 2027. Lead with the cut: the new figure, the old one, and the size of the revision. The mechanism: this is demand destroyed by price and by physical shortage, not by a weak economy alone; the war in the Gulf and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz took supply off the market, the price of Brent crude rose, and importers in Asia and Africa bought less because they could not pay or could not get cargoes; say which regions account for the cut and what OPEC assumes about Hormuz reopening in its 2027 rebound. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The accountability point: the producers' own club, several of whose members are parties to or targets in the war, is describing the shortage as deferred demand; set that against what the IEA says, if a page gives it. Who it lands on: fuel-importing countries, many of them Muslim-majority. Write from Reuters; TASS is Russian state media and is used only for the Secretary General's quoted remarks. This is a forecast: state it as OPEC's. Write your own headline. Dateline Vienna.

stories.label: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford Awarded Nobel for Economics
stories.summary: The economics Nobel went on Monday to Robert Hall and Michael Woodford, two American macroeconomists whose work, the committee said, left policymakers 'better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy'. Lead with the award and that citation, then teach the ideas, which is the value of this piece: Woodford's framework is the one central banks actually run, in which the interest rate, not the money supply, is the tool, and what moves the economy is the public's expectation of future rates, which is why the Fed and the ECB publish 'forward guidance'; Hall's work on how households spend out of expected lifetime income, and on why unemployment swings so far in recessions, as the pages give it. Explain each in two plain sentences with one concrete example. The timing is the point: the prize for managing shocks lands in the largest energy supply shock on record, with central banks raising rates into a war; name the series plainly, the Fed's and the ECB's policy rates, and say what the laureates' models do and do not say about a supply shock that rates cannot fix. One clause: the prize is the Swedish central bank's, added in 1968, not one of Alfred Nobel's. Dateline Stockholm.

stories.label: Food thrown out: cyberattack defrosts fridges in 200 French supermarkets
stories.summary: A cyberattack switched the refrigeration in French supermarkets into defrost, spoiling food in some 150 to 200 Intermarché shops and almost 100 Coopérative U outlets, plus other chains, and causing fires, the retailers told AFP on Monday. Lead with the physical result: an intrusion that destroyed stock and started fires in hundreds of buildings at once. The mechanism for a technical reader: the fridges were not hacked one by one; supermarket cold rooms are run by networked controllers managed remotely by a refrigeration contractor or a cloud platform, so one compromised supplier account reaches every store it serves; say which system or vendor was hit, how the attackers got in, whether it was ransomware, sabotage or a claimed action, and how the fires started, only as the page gives it, and say plainly what is not yet known. Give the scale in stores, tonnes or euros if stated, and what ANSSI or prosecutors have opened. The structural point: building-management and industrial control systems are the soft edge of the food supply, shared across competing chains through a common vendor. The page is AFP copy carried by the SCMP: attribute to AFP and the retailers. Single source. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: AI Company Lets Cops Pinpoint Specific Houses Based on a Single Interior Photo
stories.summary: Raven, the company formerly called GeoSpy, sells police a tool that takes one photo of a room and returns the specific Airbnb or Zillow property it was taken in, 404 Media reports. Lead with the capability in one concrete sentence: a washer-dryer, a countertop or a window frame in the background of a picture is enough to produce an address. The mechanism for a technical reader: the system has indexed the interior photos of rental and for-sale listings, tens of millions of homes photographed room by room and published by their owners, and matches a query image against that index; say how the index was built (scraping, and whether Airbnb and Zillow consented or object), what accuracy Raven claims, which agencies have bought it and for what, and what legal process, if any, a search requires. The accountability point: a listing made to rent or sell a home has become a permanent police lookup table for its interior, and it is the old GeoSpy outdoor-geolocation tool turned indoors, sold to law enforcement with no warrant standard. Give Raven's, Airbnb's and Zillow's replies as 404 Media has them. 404 Media's companion podcast item ('Cops can creep on Airbnb') is the same story: do not use it separately. Single source. Dateline as the report places Raven. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Sensible Grindr-Daten: Microsoft-Tochter muss Rekordstrafe zahlen
stories.summary: Xandr, the advertising-technology company owned by Microsoft, is to pay the largest data-protection fine in Norway's history for passing sensitive data about Grindr users on to numerous other ad firms, netzpolitik.org reports. Lead with the fine (amount in kroner and euros, the authority, Datatilsynet, and whether it is final or appealable) and what was shared. The mechanism for a technical reader: in real-time bidding, an app sends a 'bid request' with a device ID, location and the app's name to an ad exchange, which broadcasts it to hundreds of bidders; when the app is Grindr, the app name alone reveals sexual orientation, a special category under GDPR Article 9 that needs explicit consent; say what Xandr did with the requests, how many recipients and users were involved, and how this follows the earlier Norwegian fine on Grindr itself and the complaint by the consumer council and noyb. The accountability point, attributed to the data-protection and consumer advocates quoted: the fine reaches the middleman exchange, not only the app, which is the part of the ad industry that had escaped. Who it lands on: users in countries where being identified as gay is dangerous or criminal. In German; translate names and figures exactly and attribute to netzpolitik.org and the authority. Give Microsoft's or Xandr's reply. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Oslo.

stories.label: Atypical B cells shift immune roles as they develop, malaria study finds
stories.summary: A study of malaria reports how 'atypical' B cells arise and what they do: they change immune roles as they mature, which may settle a long argument over whether these cells are exhausted bystanders or working parts of the response. Lead with the finding in plain words. The mechanism for a technical reader: B cells make antibodies; atypical B cells pile up in people repeatedly infected with malaria, and also in HIV, lupus and after some vaccinations, and it has been unclear where they come from and whether they help or hinder; say what the team found at each stage of the cells' development, in whom or in what model (patients in an endemic area, volunteers, mice), with which methods (single-cell sequencing, lineage tracing), and how large the study was. Why it matters: immunity to malaria builds slowly and fades, and vaccines against it protect only partly; knowing whether these cells aid or blunt the antibody response bears on vaccine design, which is the authors' suggestion and not a result. Malaria kills about 600,000 people a year, most of them African children (attribute to WHO). Name the authors, institution and journal, and state the limits they give. This is a press-release rewrite: read the page and, if it links the paper, claim no more than the paper does. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline the city of the lead institution.

stories.label: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
stories.summary: A brain-imaging study in Nature Communications maps, person by person, where imagined pain and real pain overlap in the brain and where they part. Lead with the answer in plain words: how much of the brain's response to actually being hurt is reproduced when a person only imagines it, and which regions respond to the real thing alone. The mechanism for a technical reader: most fMRI studies average many brains and blur individual anatomy; 'precision functional mapping' scans a few people for many hours each, so each person's own networks can be drawn; say how many participants, how pain was delivered and imagined, which regions and networks were shared (as the paper names them) and which were specific to felt pain, and how strong the effects were. Why it matters: imagination as simulation is a leading theory of how the brain predicts and plans, and the result bears on chronic pain, placebo effects and the claim that fMRI can 'read' pain objectively, each only as far as the authors take it. Name the authors and institutions and state the limits they give (few participants, healthy volunteers). This is an early-access accepted manuscript: read the paper first and claim no more than it does. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline the city of the lead institution.

stories.label: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas Resigns
stories.summary: Bärbel Bas quit on Monday as Germany's labour minister and as co-leader of the SPD, citing her stepdaughter's death and 'open attacks' from inside the governing coalition. Lead with the double resignation and her stated reasons, quoted exactly, then the mechanism: the junior partner in Merz's coalition loses the minister who runs the welfare and pensions budget and one of its two party leaders at once; say which disputes with the CDU preceded it (as the pages give them), who succeeds her in each post, what Lars Klingbeil and Merz said, and whether the coalition's majority or programme is at risk. Sentiment diverges: DW and Anadolu report it flatly, the Bloomberg and Reuters copies frame it as a coalition falling deeper into turmoil; say what is established and what is reading. Anadolu is Turkish state media, used where the others agree. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: France: Founder of small centre-left party wins presidential primary
stories.summary: Raphaël Glucksmann, an MEP and co-president of the small Place Publique party, has won the centre-left primary for France's 2027 presidential election, beating the Socialist Party's own figures. Lead with the result in numbers (his share, turnout, whom he beat, as the pages give them) and his line about ending 'the hegemony of brutes over the French left', quoted exactly and explained: it is aimed at Jean-Luc Mélenchon's La France Insoumise. The mechanism: the French left goes into the election split between a social-democratic candidate chosen by primary and a radical left that stayed out of it, and under the two-round system a divided left risks having no one in the run-off against the far right; say who took part in the primary, who refused, and where the polls put each, only as the pages give it. The structural point: a party with almost no members has taken over the candidacy of the party that once governed France. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: 'Unacceptable': CJP on Jantar Mantar being denotified as protest site
stories.summary: New since yesterday's pieces on the Delhi detentions, the chief justice declining to meet the opposition and the police at Dhruv Rathee's home (one clause): Delhi Police has removed Jantar Mantar, the capital's designated protest ground for decades, from the list of authorised protest sites and named Ramlila Maidan, Burari and other grounds far from parliament instead, and Rahul Gandhi is to march to the Supreme Court on Monday. Lead with the denotification: who ordered it, under what power, from when, and where protest is now allowed. The mechanism for a reader outside India: Jantar Mantar is where the courts themselves directed demonstrations be held, within sight of parliament, so moving the permitted site moves dissent out of view without banning it; say what Saurav Das of the Cockroach Janta Party said (quoted exactly), what the police give as the reason, and what the protest demands (the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the voter-roll revision). The Indian Express (https://indianexpress.com/article/india/cjp-delhi-police-protest-janatar-mantar-cec-gyanesh-kumar-10917927/) and DW's India file (https://www.dw.com/en/india-news-rahul-gandhi-to-march-to-supreme-court/live-79638649) cover the same day and the march. All cluster sources are Indian outlets. Write your own headline, and spell out the party's name: here CJP is not the chief justice. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: China sanctions Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry on Monday sanctioned Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister by name over their dealings with Taiwan. Lead with who was sanctioned, for what act (a visit, a statement, as the page gives it) and what the sanctions do in practice (entry bans, asset freezes, a bar on dealings with Chinese entities). The mechanism: Paraguay and Belize are among the dozen states that still recognise Taipei, and Beijing is moving from courting such governments to punishing their individual ministers, a tool it has so far used mostly against US and European politicians; say what each country gets from Taiwan and what China has offered or withheld (Paraguay's beef and soy exports, if the page has it), and how Asunción, Belmopan and Taipei responded. The structural point: two small Latin American and Caribbean states are being made to carry the cost of a great-power dispute personally. Al Jazeera is the one source. Dateline Beijing, with the Latin American side given its own voice.

stories.label: China Says Hybrid-Car Deal With Europe to Ensure 'Export Space'
stories.summary: China and the EU have agreed an 'upward arrangement' that ties Chinese hybrid-car sales in Europe to their 2025 level, which Beijing's commerce ministry says secures 'export space and steady growth' for its carmakers. Lead with the terms: what is capped or indexed, from which base, and for how long. The mechanism: the EU's tariffs hit battery-electric cars, so Chinese makers switched to plug-in hybrids, which the duties did not cover, and built a trade ETAuto puts at $7.5 billion; this deal closes that gap by managed quantity instead of a new tariff. Say what each side gave, what happens to the existing EV duties and minimum-price talks, and which makers (BYD, SAIC's MG, Chery) are most exposed, only as the pages give it. The structural point: Brussels and Beijing are settling a trade dispute by quota, the instrument free-trade rules were written to end, to avoid a tariff war while both face Washington. Bloomberg is paywalled; ETAuto carries the figures. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: France's Macron sees no 'energy truce on Russian side'
stories.summary: New since yesterday's pieces on Trump's announced 'energy ceasefire', the Duma member who knew nothing of it and the US threat to halt PURL arms (one clause): the truce has now been tested and, Kyiv says, broken. Zelenskiy accuses Russia of striking a thermal power plant in Kharkiv after Trump's announcement, says Ukraine's long-range strikes will continue until Moscow actually stops, and insists a truce must cover the power grid and not only oil ('we have one refinery', as the Kyiv Independent quotes him); Macron says he sees no truce on the Russian side; and the EU adopted a new sanctions round the same day (Reuters: https://sg.news.yahoo.com/ukraine-accuses-russia-violating-trumps-095008137.html). Lead with the Kharkiv strike and the accusation, attributed, and say what Moscow and Washington have said. The mechanism: the truce was announced by a third party to protect fuel prices before the US midterms, with no text, monitor or agreed scope, so each side defines it; give the sanctions round's size and targets as the pages give them. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude, which fell on the announcement and moves with every refinery strike. Who it lands on: Ukrainians facing winter on a damaged grid. Write from Reuters, Ukrainska Pravda and the Kyiv Independent; the Times of Israel link is a liveblog entry. Write your own headline. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Delta records highest oil spill as nine incidents release nearly 130,000 litres of crude
stories.summary: Nine oil spills in the Niger Delta in August and September released an estimated 129,855 litres of crude, almost 90% of it in Delta State; ND Western had the largest single spill and Renaissance, the Nigerian consortium that bought Shell's onshore business, had the most incidents. Lead with the volume and the two companies named. The mechanism: say where the figures come from (the spill regulator NOSDRA's records, as Premium Times reads them), how each spill is attributed (sabotage or equipment failure, and who makes that call, since it decides whether the operator must pay compensation), how much was recovered, and which communities, farmland and waterways were hit. The accountability point: the oil majors sold their onshore fields to local firms and left, and the spills continue under new owners with less capital and the same pipelines; state that only as far as the piece supports it. Who it lands on: fishing and farming communities of the delta. Premium Times is the Nigerian outlet and the only source. Dateline Warri or Asaba, as the report places the spills.

stories.label: Rainfall varied widely in El Nino years in T
stories.summary: The EU's Copernicus climate service says the developing El Niño set a sea-surface temperature record in a key zone of the equatorial Pacific in September, a further sign it is on course to be among the strongest ever measured. Lead with the measurement: which region (Niño 3.4 or as the page names it), the temperature or anomaly, and the record it broke. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what El Niño is (weakened trade winds let warm water spread east across the Pacific, shifting rainfall worldwide), how its strength is measured, what makes one 'super', and what forecasters expect for its peak. Then who it lands on, with the regional reports in the cluster: dry months forecast for Mindanao in the Philippines, erratic monsoon rainfall in India's Telangana, and the risk to harvests and food prices across South and Southeast Asia, southern Africa and Latin America. This is a measurement and a forecast, not a disaster report: state no impact that has not been observed or forecast by a named agency. New Scientist (https://www.newscientist.com/article/2592513-why-the-worst-el-nino-killed-millions-and-how-we-can-avoid-a-repeat/) gives the history of the 1877 event in a clause. The feed title is from the Times of India's local item: write your own headline. Dateline Bonn or Reading, wherever the report places Copernicus.

stories.label: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival - Nature Genetics
stories.summary: A study in Nature Genetics finds that when the rings of extrachromosomal DNA that drive some of the most aggressive cancers get trapped in micronuclei, small stray compartments outside the cell's main nucleus, the tumour cells do worse, and patients whose tumours show more of it survive longer. Lead with that in plain words. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what ecDNA is (circular DNA outside the chromosomes carrying extra copies of oncogenes such as MYC, inherited unevenly so tumours evolve fast and resist drugs), how replication stress pushes it into micronuclei, what happens to it there (silenced, damaged or lost, as the paper shows), and how the team showed it: cell lines, engineered mice, patient samples, single-micronucleus sequencing and live imaging. Why it matters: ecDNA cancers have had no specific weakness to target, and this suggests one, drugs that raise replication stress to drive ecDNA out of the nucleus; state that as the authors' suggestion, not a treatment. Name the authors and institutions, give the patient-survival association with its size and its limits (association, not proof of cause). Read the paper first and claim no more than it does. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline the city of the lead institution.

stories.label: Scam: Das Geschäft mit den betrügerischen Blutzuckeruhren
stories.summary: Smartwatches sold as measuring blood sugar without a needle show invented readings: one tested by Germany's consumer federation vzbv gave the same glucose value strapped to a banana as on a wrist. They were on sale at large retailers' online marketplaces, including eBay and Mediamarkt.de, and the listings came down only after netzpolitik.org sent press questions. Lead with the banana test and where the watches were sold. The mechanism for a technical reader: no consumer wearable can measure glucose optically through the skin today, so the watches derive a plausible-looking number from pulse data or nothing at all; say what the vzbv tested and found, why such a device is an unapproved medical product under EU law, and who is liable when a marketplace hosts a third-party seller (the Digital Services Act's notice-and-action duty against the platforms' own vetting claims). Who it lands on: diabetics who dose insulin on a false reading. The accountability point: enforcement worked only when a journalist asked. In German; translate names and figures exactly and attribute findings to the vzbv and netzpolitik.org. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Ledger says unauthorized implant found in at least one device sold by CryptoBilis
stories.summary: Ledger, the maker of hardware crypto wallets, has confirmed that a device tied to recent customer losses contained an unauthorised hardware implant, and that it was sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in the Philippines. Lead with the confirmation and Ledger's advice: do not initialise unused devices from that seller, and move funds from active ones to a new seed on a device bought direct. The mechanism for a technical reader: a hardware wallet's whole promise is that the private key never leaves a tamper-resistant chip, so the attack moves upstream to the box, a component added between factory and customer that leaks or pre-determines the seed; say what the implant did and how it was found, how many devices and how much money are involved, whether Ledger's genuine-check attestation caught it, and what CryptoBilis says, only as the page gives it. The structural point: it is a supply-chain attack on physical hardware, and buyers in Southeast Asia rely on resellers because direct shipping is slow or dear. CoinDesk is a trade outlet: no price commentary. Single source. Dateline Manila, or Paris if the report files from Ledger's base.

stories.label: 每秒狂喷近500个token！智谱GLM-5.3高速版悄悄亮相
stories.summary: Zhipu has quietly begun testing GLM-5.3 HighSpeed, a fast version of its flagship model, inside its coding tool ZCode, and a tester reports output above 490 tokens a second, against 70.84 for Zhipu's standard GLM-5.3 API and 121.34 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on the AI Ping benchmark, Zhidx, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, reports. Lead with the speed and its caveat: one user's figure from a limited grey-scale test, not a served-at-scale number, with no price yet. The mechanism for a technical reader: the speed-up is infrastructure, not a smaller model (the context window stays at 1 million tokens, max output 131,072); describe what Zhipu and the TileRT team did for the earlier GLM-5.1 high-speed API (a rewritten inference path, dynamic batching and KV-cache scheduling, and TileRT's approach of compiling the whole compute graph ahead of time into a persistent engine kernel resident on the GPU instead of scheduling operators at run time), and say that Zhidx infers the same for 5.3. Why it matters: a coding agent makes dozens of model calls per task, so tokens per second, not benchmark scores, sets how long the task takes, and Chinese labs are competing on serving speed with constrained hardware. In Chinese; translate figures exactly and attribute every judgement to Zhidx or the tester. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: North Korea fires missiles days after South Korea's hypersonic test
stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast at about 09:20 local time on Monday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs said, days after Seoul tested a hypersonic missile of its own. Lead with the launch as Seoul's military gives it (number, type, range, where they fell), attributed, and say what Tokyo and Washington reported. The mechanism: an action-reaction cycle in which each side's test is the other's justification; say what South Korea tested and when, what Pyongyang has said, and which UN resolutions bar the North's ballistic launches. One clause, only if a page has it: a Russian minister arrived in Pyongyang the same day. Sentiment differs little across outlets; write from Reuters and Al Jazeera, and use TASS and Mehr (Russian and Iranian state media) only where they agree. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: US arrests fugitive in $2 billion Venezuelan bribery scheme
stories.summary: Alvaro Pulido Vargas, the Colombian businessman accused with Alex Saab of bribing Venezuelan officials and laundering money skimmed from the state's subsidised food programme, has been arrested and faces federal charges in Florida. Lead with the arrest and what is not known (when and where he was taken), then the charge: who is accused of paying whom, how much (the $2 billion figure, attributed to prosecutors), and through which contracts. The mechanism: food-import contracts for Venezuelans who could not afford to eat were overpriced and the difference moved through US banks, which is what gives a Florida court jurisdiction. Who it lands on: the Venezuelans the food boxes were meant for. Say what became of Saab's own case and what Caracas has said, only as the pages give it; state the allegations as allegations. Fox News frames it through Maduro; write from the NYT account. Dateline Miami. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: US judge orders halt to taxpayer-funded promo ads of Trump
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled on Sunday night that Donald Trump must cancel the remaining television ads promoting him that were paid for with millions in public money, granting an order sought by the watchdog Common Cause weeks before the midterm elections. Lead with the order: which court and judge, what it stops and from when, and how much was spent and by which department (the feed tags Homeland Security). The mechanism: say which law bars the use of appropriated funds for political promotion, what the government argued (Trump called the ads 'positive promotion for our great USA'), and whether the ruling is temporary and will be appealed. The accountability point: an incumbent using the state's advertising budget in an election season, stopped by a private group's lawsuit, not by Congress or an inspector. Single source. Dateline as the report places the court. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: FT: US threatens to halt arms supplies to Ukraine under PURL programme
stories.summary: New since yesterday's pieces on Zelenskiy's refinery offer and the Duma member doubting Trump's 'energy ceasefire' (one clause each): Washington has moved from demand to threat. The Financial Times and Axios report that the Trump administration is threatening to stop weapons deliveries under PURL, the scheme through which NATO allies pay for US-made arms for Ukraine, and to cut intelligence sharing, unless Kyiv stops striking Russian oil refineries. Lead with the threat and its terms, attributed to the FT and Axios as Ukrainska Pravda relays them; quote the White House official ('Trump is really mad') only with that attribution. The mechanism: the weapons are bought by Europeans, so the US is withholding goods others have paid for to protect fuel prices at home before the midterms; say what PURL has delivered and what Kyiv and European buyers have said. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude, which the refinery strikes and the truce claim both move. Who it lands on: Ukrainians under attack on their grid before winter. Write from Ukrainska Pravda (Ukrainian, independent) and Dawn; RT, TASS and TRT World are state media, used only where they quote Axios or the FT. The Bloomberg link in the cluster is a different story (EU curbs on Chinese inverters): do not use it. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Bipartisan group of US senators opposes Trump's Russian diesel deal
stories.summary: A bipartisan group of US senators has told Trump to 'immediately reverse course' on allowing imports of Russian diesel, saying the decision breaks federal law and hands Moscow revenue for its war. Lead with the letter: who signed it (name the Republicans), which statute they say was violated, and what they demand. The mechanism: say what the administration lifted and why (diesel prices at home before the midterms, with the Gulf war and Hormuz squeezing supply), how much Russian diesel is involved and what it earns Moscow, only with figures the pages give, and what Congress can actually do beyond a letter. The accountability point: sanctions written into law, set aside by the executive for a price at the pump, and challenged from inside the president's own party. Distinct from the separate piece this cycle on the threat to Ukraine's arms supply (one clause at most). Sentiment diverges: note where the BBC and Politico differ on the legal question. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: War and high debt to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
stories.summary: Finance ministers and central bankers gather in Bangkok this week for the IMF and World Bank annual meetings under what the report calls the biggest energy supply shock on record, a widening Middle East war and rising interest rates. Lead with what the meetings open onto, in figures the page gives: growth forecasts, debt levels, and what the war has done to fuel costs. The mechanism: dear oil and diesel raise import bills and inflation, central banks raise rates, and governments that borrowed in dollars pay more to service debt just as revenue falls; say which countries the page names as most exposed and what the IMF and the Bank can offer them (lending, debt relief) against what they are asking for. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude and the Fed's interest rate. Who it lands on: importing countries of Asia and Africa, many of them Muslim-majority, that are party to none of the wars. This is a curtain-raiser: state no outcome and write only what is scheduled and said. Al Jazeera is the one source. Dateline Bangkok.

stories.label: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial
stories.summary: A candidate 'universal' flu vaccine, made from whole inactivated viruses and meant to protect across influenza strains instead of the few picked each season, has passed its first human trial, a randomised, placebo-controlled phase 1 study reported in Nature Communications. Lead with that in plain words and with what phase 1 does and does not show: safety and immune response, not protection. The mechanism for a technical reader: say why seasonal vaccines must be reformulated yearly (they target the fast-mutating head of haemagglutinin), what this candidate contains and why whole-virus, BPL-inactivated particles might raise broader immunity, how many volunteers there were, the doses and routes tested (the trial is double-dummy, so two routes were compared), the side effects and the breadth of the antibody and T-cell responses. Why it matters: a vaccine that need not be matched to each year's strain would matter most where annual campaigns do not reach, and in a pandemic. Name the authors, institutions and funder, and state the limits they give. Read the paper first and claim no more than it does. Single source. Dateline the city of the lead institution.

stories.label: Wildlife populations have declined 73% since 1970—but many of the world's animals still aren't being counted
stories.summary: The WWF's 2026 Living Planet Index puts the average decline in monitored wildlife populations at 73% since 1970, and the piece's point is what that number is not: it does not mean 73% of animals are gone, and many species and regions are not counted at all. Lead with the figure and its correct reading in one sentence each. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the index is built (an average of proportional changes across monitored populations, so a small population halving weighs as much as a large one), which groups and regions are over- and under-represented in the data, and how the result shifts by region or habitat (freshwater, Latin America, Africa) as the page gives it. Why it matters: the headline number steers conservation money, and the gaps fall in the tropics, where most biodiversity and the least monitoring are. Name the authors of the analysis and state the limits they give. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. Single source. Dateline the city of the lead author's institution.

stories.label: 累计43亿！国内最大AI Infra融资诞生，无问芯穹C轮拿下23亿
stories.summary: Infinigence AI (无问芯穹; confirm the English name from the page), a three-year-old Tsinghua spin-out, has closed a 2.3 billion yuan Series C, taking its total to 4.3 billion yuan, which Zhidx, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, calls the largest raise in China's AI-infrastructure sector; an IPO is reported to be in preparation. Lead with the round and what the company does, not the superlative. The mechanism for a technical reader: it owns no data centres and makes neither models nor chips; it sells the software layer that lets one model train and serve across mixed hardware, having run a 70-billion-parameter training job across four Chinese chips (Huawei Ascend, Iluvatar, MetaX, Moore Threads) and two foreign ones (AMD, Nvidia). Say why that is a necessity in China and not abroad: export controls left the country with a patchwork of accelerators, so the scheduling layer is where efficiency is won. Give the company's own performance and cost claims as claims. The structural point: state funds, Tencent, Baidu and Lenovo are all backing the same neutral layer. The piece is promotional in tone: translate figures exactly, attribute every judgement to Zhidx or the company, and leave out the valuation comparison with US firms unless stated as the outlet's view. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shanghai or Beijing, as the piece places the company.

stories.label: 10亿！上海大模型创企拿下新融资
stories.summary: MOSI (模思智能), the Shanghai company spun out of Fudan professor Qiu Xipeng's OpenMOSS group, which released China's first open ChatGPT-style model in February 2023, announced on Monday a pre-A round of more than 1 billion yuan led by Huakong Fund with a line of state-backed Shanghai funds, its second raise this year. Lead with the round and who is paying. The mechanism for a technical reader: unlike Zhipu or DeepSeek, it is not chasing general chat or coding models but real-time speech, vision and multimodal interaction for glasses, cars and robots; describe the planned MOSS Live design (a front model that keeps perceiving and talking while a back model reasons and acts), the 20-plus open-source models released in half a year, and its 'AI for AI' loop in which generative models make training data and understanding models filter it. The structural point: municipal and national state capital is funding university labs into companies, and this one publishes its weights. Translate figures exactly, attribute judgements to Zhidx, and note as the piece does that commercial use is unproven. Distinct from this cycle's piece on Infinigence (no cross-reference needed). Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: Meta Muse引爆的这场“代理人战争”，字节和腾讯都坐不住了
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports that Meta's Muse has set off what its headline calls an 'agent war', and that ByteDance and Tencent are now moving in response. The feed carries only the headline and one line, so read the page first and lead with the concrete events: what Meta shipped and when, and what ByteDance and Tencent have each announced or are reported to be building, with dates and product names. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what kind of agent Muse is and where it runs (inside a social or messaging app with a billion-plus users, if the piece says so), and why that threatens companies whose business is the same kind of super-app, WeChat and Douyin. The structural point, if the piece makes it: the contest over agents is moving from the model makers to whoever owns the place people already spend their time, and China's two largest platforms read a US rival's launch as a threat at home. In Chinese; translate names and figures exactly and attribute every judgement to TMTPost. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Beijing or Shenzhen, as the piece gives it.
